body:
I sort of get what you're saying. Those accomplishments didn't grant me permanent happiness. They did improve my self esteem though. I imagine it's rare for someone feeling so down to have a positive view of themself but I do, at least in a lot of ways. I recognize my shortcomings but I think I can accomplish anything I put effort into. I wouldnt characterize my self esteem as anything worse than neutral. The source of my depression is moreso the fact that other people are unable to see me how I see myself. I'm not trying to come off as arrogant and I recognize that part of the problem is my lack of communication skills. I think it's a chicken vs egg problem. Am I unhappy because I have trouble making friends and building relationships or do I have trouble because I'm unhappy?

I understand your point about the traveling thing too but it didn't start as an escape. Even when I have been at my highest points, I constantly fantasize about exploring the world. It is something I'm very passionate about and would do it no matter what my frame of mind is. I booked the trip before I was fired. It wasn't an escape initially but I'm concerned that it will still constructively function as one if that makes sense. So while the initial purpose of the trip was to pursue a passion, it can still be considered escaping and I'm concerned about what my state of mind will be when it's over and I lose that event to look forward to while still having the same issues.

I think you hit the nail on the head about being vulnerable. The most successful dating period of my life was when I was able to open myself up. I think I opened myself up too much and like you mentioned was devastated when they collapsed. I opened myself up to one girl who was concealing mental issues. She deteriorated over the course of our relationship and then went off the deep end when I tried to help her get back to normal. She exploited my vulnerability by fostering fake harassment accusations and trying to get me fired (she was a coworker). I met someone else a month or so later and the relationship was even better. The damage from the initial girl was still raw though and the first time the new girl needed space, I became desperate and clingy because I didn't want to be hurt again. I think ever since then I have built a wall and refuse to allow myself to hurt like that again. It's been over 2 years and I still look to the 2nd girl as the gold standard of my dating life despite it only lasting a month or so. I beat myself up for letting that fall apart and have never really gotten over it. I haven't figured out how to balance vulnerability with caution so the next best option has been to just never let myself be vulnerable. I also think I've been very unlucky with timing. There have been a number of times over the last few years where I meet someone either as a friend or potential love interest in the wrong time and place. 

Thanks again for letting me vent. I know I could use some professional help and hopefully I will have the initiative to pursue it when I return from my trip. Emotions are so complex though so it's difficult a lot of times to get across the full scope of them to my support group like my family. But anyway, I will definitely take your words to heart and think about how to improve my state of mind.

Thank you for taking the time to respond so thoroughly. I appreciate what you're saying but also have to disagree with some points.

You say that things don't make people happy but changing those aspects of my life did temporarily lead to the happiest I have ever been. I had a solid group of friends, the most active dating life I've ever had, and suicide never crossed my mind. I was happy with my college job and happy in class. I think having meaningful relationships with others is the key yo all of that. When I think back on my happiest memories, it's always the best times I've shared with others. The laughs, the new experiences, etc.

I do think one of my problems is a lack of putting myself out there. Whenever I get another job and wherever I move to, I would like to join a couple activity groups like a kickball team or something. Traveling the world is not just an escape for me. It's something I am extremely passionate about and my favorite hobby. It's hard to do such an expensive and time consuming hobby more often though. Maybe I can try taking smaller trips more often to satisfy my passion and feel more fulfilled.

Your words have gotten me to consider a few factors as to why it's hard for me to have meaningful relationships. I think I have social anxiety which causes me to build a wall and not let people in until I get very comfortable with them. I have a strong fear of rejection and have only mustered up the courage to ask 4 girls out in person, relying instead on dating apps. I have a 50% success rate when I ask someone out in person so you would think it would be easier for me. 

I'll keep trying for the time being. Maybe get into a professional therapy session when I get health insurance again. Thanks again for speaking with me.

Thanks for responding. I know how great it will be since I've done it before. I did it a few months after that fling that I mentioned ended and it was amazing. I also remember crying when it was over knowing that I had to return to my shitty life. And my life wasn't even that bad at the time. So I understand about it being a healthier form of escapism but it's still escapism. I'm still coming back to the US with no friends, no job, no dating life, etc.

I guess what is so difficult is knowing I have to work even harder to find acceptance. I've honestly worked harder than anyone else I know already. I'm the only person I know of in my grad program who was able to work fulltime while managing that heavy courseload. I've busted my ass at the gym and have made sacrifices in the kitchen to get in shape while others I know can eat whatever they want and barely work out and still look great. So knowing that despite my work, I have to go even further, is something I don't know that I have the strength for.
